Team —

Elena from NovaFlex wants a firm compute allocation for a 12-month reserved commit (deal NF-2027-Q4-01). Raw asks below; please validate and produce a conservative recommended allocation plus an ops playbook (warm-up, cache preloads, fallback variants):

Assumptions (fill/update):
- Model: llama3-13b (FP16 baseline), customer is ok with int8 quantization for inference
- Monthly generated tokens: 1.2B tokens (generation only), average generation length 100–140 tokens; prompt prefixes average 40 tokens
- Traffic profile: sustained baseline across day, peak multiplier 6x for 20 min/hour across business hours; concurrency pattern ~15k requests/day but bursty
- SLO target: p95 <= 300 ms for interactive endpoints (we should aim p95 <= 275ms before network overhead)
- Desired headroom: recommend 20–30% initially; call out cost tradeoffs for lower headroom

Deliverables requested: 
1) tokens/sec sustained baseline and tokens/sec burst numbers mapped to GPU count and GPU SKU (A100-80 / H100 equivalents)
2) p95 latency expectations per configuration and where we expect SLO violations to occur
3) fallback / canary variants (int8 smaller model) and the compute delta for those
4) timeline to provision and recommended safety margins (slab vs on-demand burst)

Ben — can you produce a calculation + spreadsheet with the per-GPU tokens/sec estimate, assumptions (seq len, kv cache hit rate, batching), and recommended committed slab counts? Vanessa — pricing and procurement gating (lead times, DocuSign) — can you add the commercial notes and approve a small provisioning credit if needed? Marissa — any exec-level exceptions for SLA or discounts?

Thanks,

From: ben_carter
To: dylan_brooks, vanessa_ortiz, marissa_cole
Date: 2027-11-15 14:05 UTC
Subject: Re: NovaFlex sizing — initial model and numbers (attachment)

Folks — attached is a first-pass workbook (nova_compute_model_v1.xlsx). Summary here with the assumptions I used:

Key modeling assumptions:
- Model profile: Llama3-13B quantized to int8; effective tokens/sec per A100-80 equiv GPU: 1500 tokens/sec sustained at 128 seq, 2.2k tokens/sec at 64 seq (lower latency paths)
- Average generation token length assumed: 100 tokens; prompt prefix caching estimated hit-rate 28% (prefix reuse from templates)
- Effective per-request latency breakdown: decode + kernel exec ~140–180ms (varies by seq), network & orchestration ~40–60ms, p95 target cushion -> aim for kernel path p95 <= 220ms

Compute reconciliation (recommended):
- Sustained baseline tokens/sec required: (1.2B tokens / 30 days) / (24*3600) ≈ 463 tokens/sec sustained generation. Accounting for prefix cache and batched efficiency assume net required per-second load ≈ 340 tokens/sec.
- Peak design target (6x business-hour spikes): peak tokens/sec ≈ 2040 tokens/sec.

Slab sizing (A100-80 equivalents):
- Baseline slab to meet sustained with 25% headroom: 1 GPU gives 1500 tokens/sec capacity; but to accommodate distribution and failure domains we recommend a minimum committed slab of 3 GPUs (primary pool) to achieve 4.5k tokens/sec capacity (this gives ~120% headroom over peak).
- Cost-efficient commit alternative: 2 GPUs + 2 GPU burst (on-demand) — steady-state OK, but riskier for sustained 6x spikes.

SLO fit & notes:
- With 3x A100 slab and our batching + prefix cache assumptions, expected p95 (gateway to user) ≈ 240–270ms. This meets the <=300ms SLO with a safety margin. If NovaFlex insists on p95 <=250ms we should add one more GPU (4 total) or move to lower-latency kernel set (64 seq optimized) which reduces effective tokens/sec per GPU to 2.2k but increases cost per token slightly.

Fallback strategy:
- Canary variant: llama3-7b-int8 (≈40% fewer tokens/sec per GPU) — shift 20% of traffic to this variant during sustained peaks to avoid SLO breaches.
- Cache-first routing: route requests with cached prefixes to a dedicated hot pool (1 GPU) to further shave p95 on interactive flows.

Provisioning timeline:
- Reserved slab: 2–4 business days after contract & payment clears for dedicated provisioning; burst/on-demand instant.

I've included a worked spreadsheet and a one-page proposal PDF. Please review and flag anything you want tightened before I send to Elena.

(attachment: nova_compute_model_v1.xlsx)

Ben Carter
Capacity Modeling, Redwood Inference
